queries.hook: The wish to understand what these texts teach, and to find in them something steady to lean on.
queries.diagnose: When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass.
queries.steady: What passes cannot fill the heart; turning toward what lasts gives each day a quiet purpose.
queries.act: Turn toward what lasts: serve, study, reflect daily, and offer your work to something beyond yourself.
queries.story: A story of a student who came to a teacher with questions and was led, step by step, toward the truth.

hook.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
hook.setting: Letter from Alameda, California, 18 April 1900, after laying down his role as leader.
hook.line: I am glad I was born, glad I suffered so, glad I did make big blunders, glad to enter peace.
hook.translation: I am glad I was born, glad I suffered so, glad I did make big blunders, glad to enter peace.
hook.why: Honest looking back, with gratitude for the mistakes, can bring peace.

prasang.title: 'I am drifting': a letter from Alameda (1900)
prasang.summary: Two years before his death, worn out, he writes that he has laid down the role of leader. He is glad he was born, glad he suffered, glad he made big blunders. He admits that ambition, personality, fear and love of power lay behind his work, and says they are fading as he drifts toward peace.
prasang.lesson: Honest looking back, with gratitude for the mistakes, can bring peace.

hook.for_you: You want to hold on to this feeling, and this verse is glad to enter peace.

alternates.speaker: Bhishma
alternates.setting: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma how an eldest brother should treat his younger brothers, and they him.
alternates.sanskrit: दशाचार्यानुपाध्याय उपाध्यायान्पिता दश / दश चैव पितॄन्माता सर्वां वा पृथिवीमपि / गौरवेणाभिभवति नास्ति मातृसमो गुरुः
alternates.line: There is no teacher like a mother.
alternates.translation: A teacher outweighs ten instructors, a father ten teachers, and a mother ten fathers, even the whole earth. There is no teacher equal to a mother.
alternates.why: Overlook small faults, correct gently, share fairly, and don't let outsiders divide you.

prasang.title: Bhishma on elder and younger siblings
prasang.summary: Yudhishthira asks how the eldest brother should treat the younger ones. Bhishma: overlook small faults and correct gently, beware outsiders who sow division, divide property equally, and honour the mother above all.
prasang.lesson: Overlook small faults, correct gently, share fairly, and don't let outsiders divide you.

alternates.speaker: Bhartrihari
alternates.setting: From 'Worship of Shiva': gratitude for a simple life.
alternates.sanskrit: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
alternates.line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
alternates.translation: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
alternates.why: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Worship of Shiva
prasang.summary: Devotional verses longing for a quiet life by the Ganga in Shiva's presence, including a famous non-sectarian line that Shiva and Vishnu are one in essence.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Do the work steadily, letting go of clinging. Stay the same in success and failure; that balance is yoga.
verse.translation: Established in yoga, do your work, Dhananjaya, giving up attachment, the same in success and failure. This evenness is called yoga.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: Even in success and failure doesn't mean indifferent to them; learn from both without being thrown.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.for_you: Now steady your heart in this joy, letting go of the need to hold on, and stay even as the days unfold.
verse.try_today: Notice one small act today done without wanting anything back.
verse.scene_line: You stand with the new life beside the steady path, offering thanks without attachment to the outcome.

why: Your part is the work (Bhagavad Gita 2.47-50)

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on worship for rewards and worship without desire.
verse.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते । तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥
verse.line: Turn to me with your whole heart, and I will carry what you lack and guard what you have.
verse.translation: To those who think of me alone and worship me, ever devoted, I bring what they lack and preserve what they have.
verse.why: Trust eases the worry of getting and keeping.
verse.misuse: Not 'God will pay the bills, so don't plan'. Trust eases worry; it doesn't replace effort or prudence.

prasang.title: Worship with and without desire, and their fruits
prasang.summary: Those who worship for heavenly rewards return when merit runs out; those who think of him alone are carried and protected.
prasang.lesson: Trust eases the worry of getting and keeping.

verse.for_you: Yesterday steadied you in letting go. Today, the joy of your granddaughter is held by a care that never lets go, and what you have is already kept safe.
verse.try_today: Rest in the knowledge that what you hold is already kept.
verse.scene_line: You stand with a healthy granddaughter and a healthy child, and you are met with a vow to keep what you have.

why: Rama's vow of safety to whoever comes afraid; 'I carry what they lack'.

verse.speaker: Sumitra
verse.setting: Sumitra tells her son Lakshman to follow Ram into exile.
verse.sanskrit: अवध तहाँ जहँ राम निवासू। तहँइँ दिवसु जहँ भानु प्रकासू॥ जौं पै सीय रामु बन जाहीं। अवध तुम्हार काजु कछु नाहीं ॥
verse.line: Home is wherever your people are, as day is wherever the sun shines.
verse.translation: Ayodhya is wherever Ram lives; day is wherever the sun shines. If Sita and Ram really go to the forest, you have nothing to do in Ayodhya.
verse.why: Home is where your people are; a good send-off gives values, not just tears.

prasang.title: Sumitra sends Lakshman with Ram
prasang.summary: Ram asks Lakshman to stay and care for their old father and grieving mothers; Lakshman cannot imagine life apart from him. He goes to his mother Sumitra, afraid she will stop him. Instead she tells him that home is wherever Ram is, as day is wherever the sun shines, and gives him one piece of advice for the road.
prasang.story_hook: Lakshman went to his mother expecting to be told to stay.
prasang.lesson: Home is where your people are; a good send-off gives values, not just tears.

verse.for_you: Today, your granddaughter’s joy is held by a care that never lets go, and what you have is already kept safe. Home is wherever your people are, as day is wherever the sun shines.
verse.try_today: Notice one place where your people are and let it feel like home.
verse.scene_line: You stand in gratitude beside Sumitra, who sees home in Ram’s presence and sends him forth.

why: she sends her son to serve
where the Lord is, there is one's place

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
verse.sanskrit: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् । यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् ॥
verse.line: Whatever you do, eat, give or endure, do it as an offering.
verse.translation: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give, whatever austerity you practise, Kaunteya, do it as an offering to me.
verse.why: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.

prasang.title: The glory of selfless devotion
prasang.summary: A leaf, flower, fruit or water offered with love is accepted. Offer everything you do; the divine hates no one, and even a wrongdoer who turns wholeheartedly is counted good.
prasang.lesson: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.

verse.for_you: Yesterday home was where your people are. Today, let your gratitude become the offering itself, the simple act of giving thanks. This gratitude is a gift you hand back to the world.
verse.try_today: Give your thanks as an offering before you speak them.
verse.scene_line: In your quiet room, you hold the news of your granddaughter and offer it back with thanks.

why: each meal and gift is handed back

verse.speaker: Sampati
verse.setting: The monkeys despair at the ocean; the old vulture Sampati rouses them.
verse.sanskrit: पापिउ जाकर नाम सुमिरहीं। अति अपार भवसागर तरहीं॥ तासु दूत तुम्ह तजि कदराई राम हृदयँ धरि करहु उपाई ॥
verse.line: Drop your timidity. Keep Ram in your heart and find a way.
verse.translation: Even sinners who remember his name cross the boundless ocean of the world. You are his messengers: give up your timidity, keep Ram in your heart and find a way.
verse.for_you: Today, hold it in your heart as you hold her. This feeling is your way forward.
verse.try_today: Let your thanks become the offering itself, a quiet gift given back to the world.
verse.scene_line: You hold the new life of your granddaughter and feel the world open before you.

why: act with Ram held in the heart

story.title: Sumitra sends Lakshman with Ram
story.story_hook: His mother did not ask him to stay; she told him how to make the forest home.
story.summary: As the exiles leave, Lakshman's mother blesses him: treat Ram as your father, Sita as your mother, and the forest as home. She tells him to go happily.
story.lesson: Home is the people you are with; you can carry it into any wilderness.
story.hook_title: Lakshman's mother Sumitra didn't ask him to stay
story.teaser: Lakshman's mother Sumitra didn't ask him to stay
story.for_you: You let go of timidity to hold this new life. Service chosen freely, described in concrete tasks, is a form of love. You have given your thanks, and now you rest in the quiet joy of it.
